notes: Companion to customers_addresses.json, which covers Billing_Address/Shipping_Address/Country. This spec covers the fields from customers_field_mapping.csv that have a clean, unambiguous transform. Three fields from that CSV are deliberately NOT encoded here because the mapping decision itself is still open, not just an unresolved lookup: Email/Phone_Number (which ADDRNUMBER series they attach to isn't decided), Is_Active (LOEVM vs SPERR semantics aren't decided), and Account_Manager_ID (the BUT050 relationship category may not be a standard delivered one). Encoding a guess for any of those would produce output that looks loadable but isn't -- see customers_field_mapping.csv and customers_worked_example.md for the open questions. BP NUMBERING CONVENTION: Business Partner staging keys are derived, not raw legacy IDs -- customers take the EVEN series (Customer_ID x 2), vendors the ODD (Vendor_ID x 2 + 1) -- because raw IDs collide in BUT000 (customer 1 vs vendor 1). Every PARTNER/KUNNR/LIFNR staging key in every spec uses the same derivation so document references resolve; a real load allocates BP numbers from a configured number range instead.

dropped_fields.reason: Duplicates CRM>Contact Persons, which is properly modeled as its own Business Partner + BUT050 relationship. This flat text field is a denormalization artifact of the source design.

Belongs in ADR6 (E-Mail Addresses), linked via ADDRNUMBER -- but which address series (billing, shipping, or a third 'standard' address) it attaches to is an open decision, not a lookup gap. See customers_worked_example.md.
Belongs in ADR2 (Telephone Numbers), same ADDRNUMBER-routing question as Email.

SAP has no matching boolean; inactivity maps to a block/deletion indicator on KNB1 (LOEVM vs SPERR), and the source data doesn't say which the legacy system meant. Picking the wrong one is a real functional difference, not a formatting choice -- needs a business decision before encoding.

Would be a BUT050 relationship (same pattern as Sales_Rep_ID and Manager_ID in the other examples), but the relationship category for 'account manager' may not be a standard SAP-delivered one -- confirm with the target system's Business Partner configuration before encoding.
